items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I took lessons from Barney Bigard.

ctx.x: How long did you play clarinet?
Didn’t play. I just took some lessons. I took lessons from Barney Bigard.
How long did you take lessons?

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: So I went to see Barney Bigard, and he gave me a little book, and I started figuring out them notes

ctx.x: So my Uncle Paul has got a clarinet. He's foolin' around with the clarinet. Can't play it. He's foolin' around, but he's learning to... I found out later that he was learning so he could count, count notation to write, because he wanted to write. So he figured he'd play a little melody and he'd be able to. So he let me blow the clarinet. A lift-off(?) point. He told me, 'Go take some lessons.'

So he sent me to Barney Bigard. They were working at ...(?)... So I went to see Barney Bigard, and he gave me a little book, and I started figuring out them notes -- and they still all, some of them, the same to me today. So I worked with him for about what...about three months -- when I could catch him. But my God, he would sit down and play

items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: so I take a half a dozen lessons to the planet with Bonabee God.

ctx.x: Who did Lloyd Arthur Dog play with?

He played with the Arnold Brass Band. They played first clarinet. He died young with a social disease. My great-aunt term. He was a shy boy. He was a basketball sergeant. Some sportswoman enticed him and got in a corral and contacted his disease. And they wouldn't tell the old folks that he was sick. And somehow they detected that he had this trouble. And when they found out about it and rushed him to the hospital, it was too late. So he died of this sickness. And this is just a lot on the planet. So Michael Paul…
Back to Florida for a minute. What were the bands like in Florida other than the band you were with?
